reference: Runnable expectations are Bash builtin metadata and the pinned flock loadable's documented interface in /source/loadables/flock.c (flock_doc, flock_struct.short_doc, and its --version string); no expectation was copied from candidate output. Operation semantics for deferred cases are referenced to GNU util-linux flock(1) and Linux flock(2), but those cases are intentionally not executed under the explicit safety instruction.
coverage: Bash reports flock as a builtin with type -t.
Bash help contains the documented FD and file command forms and principal options.
Bash short help exposes the registered synopsis.
The loadable's documented version metadata is stable.
exclusions: No lock, unlock, wait, contention, or child-command operation is executed; these remain DEFERRED as explicitly required.
No host paths, external lock peers, real network targets, privileged resources, or stress timing are used.
Operation comparisons require a future disposable Linux VM with GNU util-linux flock and synchronized private fixture processes.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash registers flock as a builtin using the Bash type -t contract.
Check the full Bash help text against the pinned documented forms, option spellings, and conflict behavior without invoking a lock operation.
cases.script:
h=$(help flock) || exit 1
[[ $h == *"Manage advisory file locks via flock(2)."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] FD"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] FILE command [args...]"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *'flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] FILE -c "shell command"'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"--shared"* && $h == *"--exclusive"* && $h == *"--unlock"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"--nonblock"* && $h == *"--wait"* && $h == *"--conflict-exit-code"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"--close"* && $h == *"--no-fork"* && $h == *"--command"* ]] || exit 1
printf 'documented-help-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check Bash help -s output against the synopsis registered in flock_struct.short_doc and Bash help builtin formatting.
cases.stdout: flock: flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] [-E N] FD | FILE [command [args] | -c CMD]

cases.purpose: Check the loadable's documented version response; --version exits before opening an operand or acquiring a lock.
Future comparison of FD form default exclusive locking, caller-shell lock lifetime, and explicit unlock on one open file description.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM with a private relative lock file, GNU util-linux flock(1) as the independent oracle, and two synchronized child processes. Verify that a lock taken on an FD remains held after the builtin returns, that a competing nonblocking attempt fails while held, and that explicit unlock releases it. Use bounded synchronization and never a host lock path.

cases.purpose: Future comparison of shared/shared compatibility, exclusive conflicts, nonblocking failure status, and the configured conflict exit code.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM, GNU util-linux flock(1), and independently synchronized processes using only a relative fixture file. Exercise shared locks, then exclusive contention with -n and -E; compare statuses and child markers. All waits must be bounded, and the fixture must be private to the VM.

cases.purpose: Future comparison of -w timeout failure and successful acquisition after a competing process releases the lock.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM with GNU util-linux flock(1), a private fixture file, and a synchronized holder process. Check both a held-past-deadline timeout and release-before-deadline acquisition with a small fractional timeout and generous bounded scheduling margins; do not use unbounded waits or stress timing.

cases.purpose: Future comparison of file-form lock-file creation, argv and -c command execution, child status propagation, and lock release after the command exits.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM with GNU util-linux flock(1), /bin/sh, and a temporary relative fixture directory. Compare stdout, exit status, lock-file contents/mode, command argument handling, and whether a second process can acquire after the child exits. Keep all command side effects inside that private directory.

cases.purpose: Future comparison of -o descriptor closure before child execution and -F no-fork exec/status behavior, including the incompatible -Fo combination.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM, GNU util-linux flock(1), private fixture files, and bounded child commands that inspect only their own inherited descriptors and write only relative markers. Compare descriptor visibility, exec failure statuses, parent-shell survival where applicable, and lock release. No process-wide signals or host process inspection are needed.

cases.purpose: Future comparison of invalid FD, malformed timeout/conflict-exit values, missing operands, and file-open error behavior without unintended lock side effects.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM with GNU util-linux flock(1) and a private relative fixture directory so parser and open-error cases can be compared for status, diagnostics, and whether a target file was created. Use only deliberately missing relative names and invalid numeric arguments; do not reference host paths.
